correctness.rationale: For s≥4, d≥3, and p∤d, a zero coordinate at a Jacobian point forces all its predecessors to vanish. On the projective torus the monomial map's character cokernel has one generator with sole effective relation Q; the Jacobian equations on its target cut out exactly a reduced point when p divides Q and the empty scheme otherwise. Euler's identity eliminates F. The fiber is a μ_|Q|-torsor, yielding m support points with local algebra k[ε]/(ε^{p^v}). At a critical point the ordinary chart Hessian is congruent to the restriction of EᵗDE in multiplicatively rescaled tangent coordinates; its radical in the full space is E⁻¹(k·1), spanned by the radial vector and ker E, so the chart Hessian has rank s−2. The exceptional case is necessarily odd characteristic, so this gives multiplicity two. Finiteness of the singular support excludes any repeated factor as well as intersections of distinct factors; a single smooth point by itself would not prove reducedness. Serre's criterion then applies. An independent enumeration of the normalized torus in the three stated fields gave support counts 1, 1, 3 and ordinary chart Hessian ranks 2, 3, 4. The two displayed Gröbner presentations were checked by substituting their triangular expressions modulo z^5−2 and z^11−4: the t_i are respectively (2,4,3,1)z² and (5,3,4,9,1)z² and satisfy all Jacobian ratios. The already proved lengths give equality of the resulting chart quotients. The supplied script was inspected, not executed; its extra excluded-characteristic finite-field check is not evidence for an all-characteristic result.

value.rationale: For a standard cyclic family, the result gives the entire bad-reduction singular scheme from an integer and distinguishes number of support points, local thickness, and quadratic rank.
